rules.title: New Jersey Security Deposit Law
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay tenants the interest earned on security deposits, give written notice of where the deposit is held, and return the deposit with interest less itemized deductions within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Wrongful withholding exposes the landlord to double damages.
rules.key_value: Return within 30 days of termination; 5 business days if displaced by fire, flood or condemnation; 7% per annum if notice or interest is not provided
rules.penalty: Tenant may recover double the wrongfully withheld amount plus costs and attorney's fees; civil penalty of $500 to $2,000 per offense for willfully withholding deposits of tenants receiving government assistance; disorderly person offense for unlawful use of deposit monies
rules.status_basis: Described as existing state law in the Landlord-Tenant guide

coverage.summary: Applies to residential rental security deposits generally; seasonal rentals are treated separately.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Seasonal use or rental is addressed, with the landlord bearing the burden of proving seasonal use.

rules.quoted_span: Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1).

rules.title: Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law
rules.requirement: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent control ordinances for 30 years after completion of construction. New Jersey has no state rent control, and municipalities may adopt rent control.

exempt_if.text: for a period of 30 years following completion of construction of the building

coverage.summary: Exempts newly constructed multiple dwellings from local rent control.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Buildings less than 30 years since completion are exempt from local rent control; government-subsidized rents may also be exempt.

precedence.text: newly constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period of 30 years

rules.quoted_span:
Under the Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law ( N.J.S.A. 2A:42 -84.5), newly 
constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period 
of 30 years following completion of construction of the building.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act (rent increase notice)
rules.requirement: Before evicting a tenant for nonpayment of an increased rent, the owner must serve a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase. The increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with municipal rent ordinances.
rules.quoted_span: This law provides that before an owner can evict a tenant for nonpayment of an increased rent, they must first serve the tenant with a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act conversion rent increase prohibition
rules.requirement: When a building is converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership, rents may not be increased to cover costs resulting solely from the conversion. Rents may still rise for new services or amenities.

requires.name: converted_building
requires.text: building converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership

coverage.summary: Applies to all tenants in converted buildings.

rules.quoted_span: If a building is converted to a condominium or cooperative form of ownership, or to fee simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover cos ts resulting solely from the conversion (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.31).

rules.title: New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (source of lawful income)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not refuse to rent or discriminate in rental on protected bases including source of lawful income. Landlords may still refuse applicants for insufficient income or poor credit history.
rules.penalty: Fines up to $10,000 for a first offense, plus monetary damages

coverage.summary: Applies to all landlord-tenant relationships except specified exemptions.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Excludes two-family owner-occupied dwellings, rooms in owner-occupied single homes, and certain single-sex or age-restricted housing.

rules.quoted_span:
The New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD), 
N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g) to -(h), prohibits discrimination when selling or renting property and requires 
equal treatment in the sale or rental of housing regardless of race, creed, color, national origin, 
ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, 
affectional or sexual orientation, gender  identity or expression, mental and physical disability, 
nationality, or source of lawful income.
